title: Qatar at the World Cup
description: They built a team from scratch to host the World Cup — how well do you know Qatar's extraordinary football journey?

questions.q: Qatar hosted the 2022 World Cup — but how did the host nation perform?
options: They won the group and reached the round of 16
They were eliminated in the group stage without winning a match
They reached the quarter-finals as hosts
They finished second in their group
questions.explain: Qatar became the first host nation to be eliminated in the group stage without winning a single match — losing to Ecuador, Senegal and the Netherlands. It was a harsh introduction to World Cup football.

questions.q: Qatar built their football programme through which famous youth academy that has produced many national team players?
questions.explain: The Aspire Academy in Doha is one of the world's best-funded sports academies, designed to create elite Qatari athletes. It was central to Qatar's football development plan and produced several key 2022 World Cup squad members.

questions.q: Qatar won the AFC Asian Cup in 2019. What was significant about this?
options: It was their first ever continental title
They became the first host nation to win the Asian Cup
They beat Japan in the final
questions.explain: Qatar won the 2019 AFC Asian Cup in the UAE — their first ever continental title. They beat Japan 3–1 in the final, with Akram Afif scoring twice. It validated their long-term football development programme.

questions.q: Qatar also won the 2023 AFC Asian Cup. Where was it held?
questions.explain: Qatar hosted and won the 2023 AFC Asian Cup on home soil, making them back-to-back Asian Cup winners. Akram Afif won the Golden Ball as best player, cementing his status as Asia's best footballer.

questions.q: Which Qatari striker is regarded as the best player ever produced by the country?
questions.explain: Akram Afif is Qatar's standout player — a left-footed winger of Yemeni heritage who plays for Al-Sadd. He won the Golden Ball at the 2023 Asian Cup and is the driving force behind Qatar's improved performances.

questions.q: In the 2022 World Cup opening ceremony and match, Qatar played Ecuador. What was the atmosphere described as?
options: The most watched opening match in World Cup history
The first World Cup opening held indoors due to the heat
Played in the state-of-the-art Al Bayt Stadium designed to look like a traditional Bedouin tent
questions.explain: The 2022 World Cup opening match was played at Al Bayt Stadium — designed to resemble a traditional Qatari Bedouin tent. Qatar lost 2–0 to Ecuador in what was a disappointing start for the hosts.

questions.q: Qatar qualified for the 2026 World Cup through which route?
options: Through the standard AFC qualifying process
questions.explain: Unlike 2022 (where they qualified as hosts), Qatar earned their 2026 place through standard AFC qualifying — a meaningful achievement that shows genuine progress beyond the host advantage.

questions.q: Qatar is one of the world's smallest nations. What is their approximate population?
questions.explain: Qatar's population is approximately 2.9–3 million, though the majority are expatriate workers. The Qatari citizen population is much smaller — around 300,000 — making their World Cup hosting and back-to-back Asian Cup wins extraordinary.

questions.q: The 2022 World Cup was the first held in the Middle East and the first held in winter. Why was it held in November-December?
options: Because Qatar's summer temperatures regularly exceed 40°C, making outdoor football dangerous
To coincide with the FIFA centenary
questions.explain: Qatar's summer temperatures regularly exceed 45°C, making playing football outdoors dangerous. Moving the tournament to November-December — with mild temperatures around 20–25°C — was a major logistical departure from World Cup tradition.

questions.q: Almoez Ali scored one of the great goals of the 2019 Asian Cup — an overhead kick in the final against Japan. What was particularly special about his tournament overall?
options: He broke the Asian Cup scoring record with 9 goals in one tournament
He scored a hat-trick in the semi-final
He became the youngest player to score in an Asian Cup final
questions.explain: Almoez Ali broke the Asian Cup record by scoring 9 goals in the 2019 tournament — surpassing the previous record of 8. His overhead kick in the final against Japan was the highlight of an extraordinary individual performance.
